titleFurigana: 学[がく]生[せい]の 一[いち]日[にち]
description: Spend a full Monday with Ken, an international student in Tokyo: the morning train, Japanese class, curry with friends at the cafeteria, the quiet library, a phone call home, and bed.
sentences: 私[わたし]の 名前[なまえ]は ケンです。
My name is Ken.
〜は〜です: topic + copula, the basic self-introduction pattern.
東京[とうきょう]の 大学[だいがく]の 留学生[りゅうがくせい]です。
I am an international student at a university in Tokyo.
の links nouns: 東京の大学 (a university in Tokyo), 大学の留学生 (a student of the university).
今日[きょう]は 月曜日[げつようび]です。
Today is Monday.
毎朝[まいあさ]、七時[しちじ]に 起[お]きます。
Every morning I get up at seven.
に after a clock time says WHEN. 毎朝 (every morning) takes no に.
朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]に パンを 食[た]べて、コーヒーを 飲[の]みます。
For breakfast I eat bread and drink coffee.
Verb て-form links actions in sequence: 食べて、飲みます.
八時[はちじ]半[はん]に 家[いえ]を 出[で]ます。
I leave the house at eight thirty.
出ます takes を for the place you leave.
駅[えき]まで 歩[ある]いて、電車[でんしゃ]に 乗[の]ります。
I walk to the station and take the train.
〜まで = up to / as far as. 〜に 乗ります = ride (a vehicle).
電車[でんしゃ]の 中[なか]は いつも 人[ひと]が たくさん います。
The train is always full of people. (There are always many people on the train.)
います is for living things (people, animals); あります is for objects.
九時[くじ]から 日本語[にほんご]の 授業[じゅぎょう]が あります。
From nine o'clock there is a Japanese class.
〜から marks the starting time; 〜が あります: something exists or takes place.
田中[たなか]先生[せんせい]は やさしい 先生[せんせい]です。
Ms. Tanaka is a kind teacher.
私[わたし]は まだ 日本語[にほんご]が 上手[じょうず]では ありません。
I am not good at Japanese yet.
〜では ありません = polite negative of です. まだ = not yet.
でも、毎日[まいにち] 勉強[べんきょう]して います。
But I study every day.
て-form + います expresses a repeated habit when a frequency word like 毎日 is present.
十二時[じゅうにじ]に 友達[ともだち]と 学食[がくしょく]で 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を 食[た]べます。
At twelve I eat lunch with my friends at the school cafeteria.
と = together with; で = the place where an action happens.
友達[ともだち]の 名前[なまえ]は メイさんと タカシさんです。
My friends' names are Mei and Takashi.
A と B = A and B (a complete list of two).
今日[きょう]は カレーを 食[た]べました。
Today I ate curry.
〜ました = polite past.
学食[がくしょく]の カレーは 安[やす]くて、おいしいです。
The cafeteria curry is cheap and tasty.
い-adjective + くて links adjectives: 安くて、おいしい.
午後[ごご]は 図書館[としょかん]へ 行[い]きます。
In the afternoon I go to the library.
へ marks the direction / destination.
図書館[としょかん]は 静[しず]かですから、私[わたし]は そこで 勉強[べんきょう]します。
The library is quiet, so I study there.
〜ですから = so / because. The reason comes FIRST.
今日[きょう]の 宿題[しゅくだい]は 漢字[かんじ]です。
Today's homework is kanji.
漢字[かんじ]は むずかしいですが、おもしろいです。
Kanji is difficult, but interesting.
〜ですが、〜 = but. This が joins two clauses; it is not the subject marker.
四時[よじ]に 学校[がっこう]を 出[で]て、コンビニへ 行[い]きます。
At four I leave school and go to the convenience store.
コンビニで おにぎりと お茶[ちゃ]を 買[か]います。
At the convenience store I buy a rice ball and tea.
で marks where the action (buying) happens.
六時[ろくじ]ごろ、うちへ 帰[かえ]ります。
Around six o'clock I go back home.
〜ごろ = around (a time). 帰ります = return (home).
よる、国[くに]の 母[はは]に 電話[でんわ]を します。
In the evening I phone my mother back in my home country.
に marks the person you phone: 母に 電話を します.
母[はは]は 「ケン、元気[げんき]ですか」と 聞[き]きます。
My mother asks, "Ken, are you well?"
「…」と 聞きます = ask "…". と quotes speech.
私[わたし]は 「元気[げんき]です。毎日[まいにち]、たのしいです」と 話[はな]します。
I say, "I'm fine. Every day is fun."
「…」と 話します = say / talk (quoting).
十一時[じゅういちじ]に ふとんに 入[はい]ります。
At eleven I get into bed (my futon).
に 入ります = enter / get into.
明日[あした]も 学校[がっこう]へ 行[い]きます。おやすみなさい。
Tomorrow I will go to school again. Good night.
も = also / again; おやすみなさい = good night.
vocab: to get up; to wake up

elements.role: Ken introduces himself with this word — it explains why a young man from abroad lives in Tokyo.
elements.mech: 留学生 = 留学 (studying abroad) + 生 (student). The suffix 〜生 turns a field into a person: 大学生 (university student), 高校生 (high-school student). Pattern: [school]の 留学生です.
ex: 私[わたし]は 日本[にほん]の 大学[だいがく]の 留学生[りゅうがくせい]です。
I am an international student at a Japanese university.

elements.role: Ken's day is organised around his Japanese class, which starts at nine.
elements.mech: 授業が あります = 'there is a class'. Use が with あります for something that exists or is scheduled. 授業 is the lesson itself — not the room (教室) and not private study (勉強).
ex: 午後[ごご]、授業[じゅぎょう]が あります。
There is a class in the afternoon.

elements.role: The reason Ken goes to the library: today's homework is kanji.
elements.mech: Students say 宿題を します (do homework); teachers say 宿題を 出[だ]します (give homework). 宿題は 〜です names what the homework is.
ex: 毎日[まいにち]、宿題[しゅくだい]を します。
I do homework every day.

elements.role: Sentence 12 shows Ken's repeated habit: he studies every single day.
elements.mech: Verb て-form + います has two jobs: an action happening now (雨が 降っています — it is raining) and a repeated habit (毎日 勉強しています). A frequency word such as 毎日 signals the habit meaning.
ex: 毎日[まいにち] 日本語[にほんご]を 勉強[べんきょう]して います。
I study Japanese every day.

elements.role: Ken explains why he studies in the library: it is quiet.
elements.mech: A ですから、B = 'A, so B'. The reason comes first and the result second — the reverse of English 'B because A'. With verbs use 〜ますから: 雨が 降りますから、…
ex: 雨[あめ]ですから、家[いえ]に います。
Because it is raining, I stay home.

elements.role: Ken admits kanji is difficult — and then says it is interesting anyway.
elements.mech: A ですが、B = 'A, but B'. Here が is a conjunction at the end of a clause, not the subject particle が. The polite form (です/ます) comes right before it.
ex: 高[たか]いですが、おいしいです。
It is expensive, but it is delicious.

elements.role: Ken's whole day is a schedule: 七時に, 十二時に, 四時に, 十一時に.
elements.mech: Put に right after a clock time or date to say WHEN something happens: 七時に 起きます. Relative words like 毎朝 (every morning) and 今日 (today) do not take に.
ex: 十時[じゅうじ]に 学校[がっこう]へ 行[い]きます。
I go to school at ten o'clock.

elements.meaning: at / in (where an action happens); by (means)
elements.role: Where Ken eats, studies and shops: 学食で, そこで, コンビニで.
elements.mech: で marks the PLACE where an action takes place (学食で 食べます) and the MEANS (電車で 行きます). Compare に, which marks where something exists or a destination.
ex: 図書館[としょかん]で 本[ほん]を 読[よ]みます。
I read books at the library.

elements.role: 学 hides in 大学, 学食, 学校 and 学生 — Ken's life is built around learning.
elements.mech: On-reading がく (大学 だいがく). In 学校 the く doubles: がく + こう → がっこう. The kun-reading まなぶ means 'to learn'. The top part of the character is a roof over a child studying.
ex: 学生[がくせい]は 学校[がっこう]で 勉強[べんきょう]します。
Students study at school.

elements.role: 電車 (train) and 電話 (phone) frame Ken's morning commute and evening call.
elements.mech: 電 is read でん in compounds: 電車 (electric car = train), 電話 (electric talk = telephone), 電気 (electricity). It never stands alone as a word. The rain radical 雨 on top hints at lightning.
ex: 電車[でんしゃ]で 学校[がっこう]へ 行[い]きます。
I go to school by train.

questions.q: 「授業[じゅぎょう]」は どんな 意味[いみ]ですか？
questions.expl: Sentence 9: 「日本語の授業があります」 — there is a Japanese class.

wrong.1: 図書館 (としょかん) is the library, where Ken goes in the afternoon (sentence 17).
wrong.2: 宿題 (しゅくだい) is homework — the thing he works on at the library (sentence 19).
wrong.3: 駅 (えき) is the station where he catches the train (sentence 7).

questions.q: 「電話[でんわ]」の 読[よ]み方[かた]は どれですか？
questions.expl: 電 is でん and 話 is わ in 電話 (phone), as in sentence 24.

wrong.1: 話 is read わ in 電話; は is only the particle sound.
wrong.2: 電 is でん (voiced で). てん would be a different character such as 天 (heaven).
wrong.3: ば is not a reading of 話; the reading here is わ.

questions.q: 「図書館[としょかん]は 静[しず]かです＿＿、そこで 勉強[べんきょう]します。」
questions.expl: から after です gives the reason: 'It is quiet, so I study there' (sentence 18).

wrong.1: が would mean 'but' — 'It is quiet, but I study there' contradicts the logic of the story.
wrong.2: と links nouns ('A and B') or means 'with'; it cannot join two clauses like this.
wrong.3: を marks a direct object, and there is no object in the first clause.

questions.q: 「漢字[かんじ]は むずかしい＿＿＿、おもしろいです。」
questions.expl: ですが = 'but'. Ken says kanji is difficult but interesting (sentence 20).

wrong.1: ですから means 'so / because'; 'Kanji is difficult, so it is interesting' does not make sense.
wrong.2: ですと is not a natural way to join these two clauses.
wrong.3: ですを is ungrammatical — を needs a verb after it.

questions.q: 「十二時[じゅうにじ]＿＿ 友達[ともだち]と 学食[がくしょく]で 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を 食[た]べます。」
questions.expl: に follows a clock time to say when something happens: 十二時に (sentence 13).

wrong.1: で marks the place or means of an action, not a clock time.
wrong.2: へ marks a direction or destination; 十二時 is a time, not a place.
wrong.3: を marks the direct object (昼ご飯), which already has its own を later in the sentence.

questions.q: ケンさんは どうして 図書館[としょかん]で 勉強[べんきょう]しますか？
opts: 図書館が 静かだから
questions.expl: Sentence 18: 図書館は静かですから — the library is quiet, so he studies there.

wrong.1: Ken eats with his friends at the cafeteria (sentence 13), not at the library.
wrong.2: The story never says his home is far away; he simply goes home at six (sentence 23).
wrong.3: 安い is used for the cafeteria curry (sentence 16), not for books.

questions.q: 学食[がくしょく]の カレーは どうですか？
opts: からくて、食べられない
questions.expl: Sentence 16: 学食のカレーは安くて、おいしいです — cheap and tasty.

wrong.1: That is the opposite: sentence 16 says it is cheap (安い) and tasty.
wrong.2: Nothing in the story says it is too spicy to eat.
wrong.3: The temperature and size of the curry are never mentioned.

questions.q: お母[かあ]さんの 「元気[げんき]ですか」は どんな 意味[いみ]ですか？
questions.expl: 元気 means well / healthy. Ken's mother checks on him in sentence 25.

wrong.1: Being hungry is a different expression (おなかが すきましたか); 元気 is about your general condition.
wrong.2: 'Busy' is 忙[いそが]しい — a different word.
wrong.3: 'Cold' is 寒[さむ]い — a different word.

questions.q: ケンさんの お母[かあ]さんは どこに いますか？
questions.expl: Sentence 24: 国の母に電話をします — his mother is back in his home country (国).

wrong.1: Ken lives in Tokyo, but his mother is in his home country, which is why he phones her.
wrong.2: The university is where Ken studies (sentence 2), not where his mother is.
wrong.3: The library is where Ken studies in the afternoon (sentence 17).
